summary.text: 小 means “small.” Its earliest documented use in this dossier is an oracle-bone example meaning “small”; the early marks behind the character are interpreted either as signs of smallness or as fine sand grains, and the evidence does not decide between them.

formation.text: The formation is disputed between an indicative account, in which marks signify smallness, and a pictographic account, in which they depict fine sand grains. The sand account has also been proposed as an early graph of 沙, but the evidence does not establish the pictured object or a sound-based borrowing. The small-seal form reflects a graphic change: the central dot became a vertical stroke between two side marks. Shuowen’s parsing of that later form as 八 plus 丨 is a historical analysis, not proof of the original construction.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are reported with three dots. In small-seal script the central dot lengthened into a vertical stroke; the curated seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image. The shape change does not identify what the earlier marks represented.

Shuowen explains the seal form as 八 and 丨, with the marks dividing something. Later analyses treat this as a reinterpretation of an altered form. Accounts also report that 小 and 少 shared an early graph and were later differentiated, but the detailed graphic and lexical relationship remains unsettled.

uncertainties.text: The early marks may signify smallness abstractly or depict fine sand grains; the dossier does not resolve this. It also does not establish the sand-grain name or pronunciation, or show that 沙 was written by borrowing 小 for a similar-sounding word.

The cited oracle-bone example 小雨 is reported as an early use, but the dossier does not provide an inspected artifact facsimile or an absolute date. It reports other old uses, including time expressions and status-related terms, without establishing their chronology or a semantic path from “small.”

小 is reported as a sound element in 雀, but the dossier does not establish the historical sound relation. Its supplied Baxter–Sagart reconstructions, *[s]ewʔ for 小 and *[ts]ewk for 雀, do not provide an obvious rhyme match in that system.

senses.text: An oracle-bone example 小雨 is reported with 小 meaning “small.” This is the earliest supported use in the dossier, not proof of the character’s hypothetical original referent.
小食 is reported as an expression for an afternoon time. The evidence does not establish how this use relates to “small.”
小采 is reported as an expression for dusk. Its chronology and relation to the “small” sense are not established.
The character is used with the sense “small,” including “tiny” and “insignificant.”

limitations.text: The dossier reports early and current uses but does not establish a dated semantic path between them or between “small” and the reported time expressions or status-related uses.

overview.text: 小 means “small.” Early marks are interpreted either as signs of smallness or as fine sand grains; the evidence does not settle which picture or sign lies behind the character.

relationships.text: Accounts report that 小 and 少 shared an early graph and later differentiated, with a lower mark in 少 becoming a diagonal stroke. The detailed graphic and lexical relationship is not settled.

小 is reported as a sound element in 雀, which is also described as contributing the sense “small bird.” This phonetic role is source-attributed; the supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 forms are 小 *[s]ewʔ and 雀 *[ts]ewk, which do not show an obvious rhyme match, and no sound-change account is established here.
